blocks.title: Welcome to Some Applications of Trigonometry
blocks.title_hi: Some Applications of Trigonometry में आपका स्वागत है
blocks.body: Before we dive in, let's look at a real-life example of this concept.
blocks.body_hi: इससे पहले कि हम शुरू करें, आइए इस अवधारणा का एक वास्तविक जीवन उदाहरण देखें।

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.body: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m away is 45°. Find the height of the tower.
blocks.body_hi: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m away is 45°. Find the height of the tower.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.body: A tower is 20√3 m tall. Find the distance from its base to a point where the angle of elevation of the top is 30° (tan 30° = 1/√3).
blocks.body_hi: A tower is 20√3 m tall. Find the distance from its base to a point where the angle of elevation of the top is 30° (tan 30° = 1/√3).

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.body: From the top of a 60 m tall cliff, the angle of depression of a boat is 30°. Find the distance of the boat from the base of the cliff (tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577).
blocks.body_hi: From the top of a 60 m tall cliff, the angle of depression of a boat is 30°. Find the distance of the boat from the base of the cliff (tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577).

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.body: The angle of elevation of the sun is 60°. Find the length of the shadow of a 15 m tall pole (tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732).
blocks.body_hi: The angle of elevation of the sun is 60°. Find the length of the shadow of a 15 m tall pole (tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732).

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.body: A ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground and its foot is 5 m from the wall. Find the height it reaches (tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732).
blocks.body_hi: A ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground and its foot is 5 m from the wall. Find the height it reaches (tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.732).

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.body: A tower stands 100 m from an observation point, with an angle of elevation of 45° to the top. Find the height of the tower.
blocks.body_hi: A tower stands 100 m from an observation point, with an angle of elevation of 45° to the top. Find the height of the tower.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.body: From a point 50 m from a building, the angle of elevation to the top is 60°. Find the height of the building (tan 60° ≈ 1.732).
blocks.body_hi: From a point 50 m from a building, the angle of elevation to the top is 60°. Find the height of the building (tan 60° ≈ 1.732).
